title: Evaluation of the Support Services for Family Caregivers Provided by Caritas Rhön-Grabfeld
summary:
Background:
Nearly 5 million people in need of care in Germany—over 80% of whom are cared for in home settings—are primarily looked after by family members, more than half exclusively by relatives who are predominantly female and aged 50–69 years.
Caring for a family member can lead to physical and mental health issues such as pain, depression, anxiety, and stress-related disorders. Women, married individuals, and those providing more than 20 hours of care per week or caring for dementia patients are particularly affected.
Health impacts of informal caregiving on family caregivers are explained through adapted stress models. Care-related stressors combined with inadequate coping strategies can trigger negative emotional, physical, or behavioral responses.

In this context, targeted therapies and empowerment programs for family caregivers are essential. The Care Realignment Act (Pflege-Neuausrichtungsgesetz) of 2012 established the legal basis for preventive and rehabilitation measures for caregivers under §23 SGB V, though few studies have scientifically evaluated their effectiveness.

Caritas Rhön-Grabfeld offers two unique nationwide projects: the Care Training Center (PflegeÜbungsZentrum, PÜZ) and the Care Training Mobile Home (PflegeÜbungsWohnmobil, PÜ-Womo), providing support and training for family caregivers and care recipients. Under §45 SGB XI, entitlement to training courses for relatives was created, largely refundable. However, the effectiveness of these measures has been evaluated in only a few studies.

The offerings at the PÜZ in Mellrichstadt extend far beyond standard caregiver training. It allows family caregivers and care recipients to test home-based care feasibility in a model apartment, including services like care coaching, hands-on care instruction, assistive device advice, and training. Trial living is possible for up to 21 days, with optional support from an affiliated outpatient nursing service.
The PÜ-Womo in Bad Königshofen, near Mellrichstadt, enables care recipients and relatives to vacation together while offering tailored support and training for caregivers.

Research Question
Through two subprojects, we aim to generate new insights into the potential effectiveness of these training and coaching measures for family caregivers and relatives. Primarily, we will investigate whether a stay at the PÜZ (Subproject 1) or PÜ-Womo (Subproject 2) can improve health aspects for caregivers/relatives and individuals in need of care.

Methodology
To this end, we will survey family caregivers and care recipients via online questionnaires before and immediately after the intervention, as well as at 6, 12, and 24 months follow-up.
conditions: Health-related, self-reported outcomes such as well-being, depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and caregiver burden in the home setting assessed by pre-post survey.

interventions.name: The primary objective of the exploratory observational study is to examine the health effects of a stay at the PflegeÜbungsZentrum of Caritas in Mellrichstadt (Subproject 1) or at the PflegeÜbungsWomo of Caritas in Bad Königshofen (Subproject 2) for family caregivers and individuals in need of care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Included will be informal and related caregivers as well as people in need of care who complete a stay at the Care Training Center (Subproject 1) or the Care Training Mobile Home (Subproject 2).
Exclusion criteria:
None.
